scenes.heading: Setting up a store that converts, not just looks nice

sents.d: Setting up a store that converts, not just looks nice
Clarity and trust matter more than visual polish.
A visually beautiful store with a confusing checkout will convert worse than a plain one that's easy to navigate.
Prioritize clear product photos from multiple angles, honest and specific descriptions, and a checkout process with as few steps and required fields as possible.
Trust signals — real reviews, a visible and simple return policy, and clear contact information — reduce the hesitation that stops first-time visitors from buying from a store they don't yet know.
Test the full purchase path yourself on both desktop and mobile regularly; a broken mobile checkout can quietly cost a large share of potential sales without ever showing up as an obvious error.

take: Make buying easy and trustworthy, and test checkout yourself.
